sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Seychelles
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate risks, sector analyses and modeled development pathways through 2050; selected sea-level results to 2100.
sources.methodology: World Bank assessment combines climate-risk, sector and economy-wide modelling.
sources.limitations: Scenario and survey-based estimates, not observed outcomes.

sources.title: Seychelles’ Third National Communication under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
sources.organization: Republic of Seychelles, Ministry of Agriculture, Climate Change and Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate communication; observed and projected sectoral risks, with precipitation simulations through 2100.
sources.methodology: Government communication compiled with ministries, local bodies and other contributors.

sources.title: UNDP Supports Stronger Early Warning Systems and Disaster Preparedness in Seychelles
sources.temporal_coverage: TIAEWS project inputs and planned disaster-information and early-warning functions reported in July 2026.
sources.methodology: Official UNDP announcement reports a project handover and stated objectives.
sources.limitations: Press release describes an input and planned functions, not evaluated results.

sources.title: About Us
sources.organization: Department of Risk and Disaster Management, Government of Seychelles
sources.temporal_coverage: Institutional history through the December 2025 transformation of DRMD into DRDM.
sources.methodology: Departmental page summarizes its statutory basis, institutional history and mandate.
sources.limitations: Institutional self-description does not evaluate operational effectiveness.

sources.title: UNDP Seychelles Country Programme Document 2024–2028
sources.temporal_coverage: UNDP country programme theory of change for 2024–2028.
sources.methodology: Official publication page provides the programme’s theory-of-change extract.
sources.limitations: The extract records programme intentions, not implementation or results.

claims.paraphrase: CCDR locates 90% of people and key infrastructure in coastal areas; heavy rain with king tides drives floods, soil/beach erosion and landslides.
claims.limitations: The national share lacks district detail.

claims.locator: CCDR printed p. 16, Table 1 and accompanying text.
claims.paraphrase: The CCDR’s regional indicator reports 2.6% at risk in Praslin/La Digue under a 1-in-20-year hazard and 15.8% in the West region under a 1-in-100-year hazard.
claims.limitations: Table says population; prose says households, leaving denominator unclear.

claims.locator: CCDR printed p. 40, road-network risk and Seychelles Land Transport Agency 2023 study.
claims.paraphrase: About 48% of roads on Mahé, Praslin and La Digue are exposed to coastal erosion/flooding; a 2023 SLTA study flags Bel Ombre, Port Glaud, Au Cap and L’Amitié Road.
After the December 2023 disaster, ASP expedited aid to 800+ households but lacks hazard targeting/geospatial data to identify Home Care clients with mobility constraints in risk areas.
affected_groups: Home Care recipients with mobility constraints
claims.limitations: The source does not attribute the December 2023 disaster to climate change.

claims.locator: TNC printed pp. 124–126, precipitation projections and Figures 3-6 to 3-8.
claims.paraphrase: At four Mahé zones and Praslin/La Digue, TNC projects little mean-annual rainfall change but 4–8 additional extreme wet days per year from a two-day historical average.
claims.scenario: ALADIN projections under SSP126, SSP245 and SSP585 through 2100.
institutions: Ministry of Agriculture, Climate Change and Environment
claims.limitations: ALADIN has high interannual variability; zones represent rainfall stations.

claims.locator: TNC printed pp. 144 and 147–148, coastal erosion and vulnerability maps.
claims.paraphrase: TNC identifies Anse Kerlan (north-west Praslin) and Anse Royale (south-east Mahé) among eroded, vulnerable beaches, citing steep reef bathymetry that lets waves break close to shore.
claims.limitations: Erosion has non-climate drivers, including mining and construction.

claims.locator: TNC printed pp. 160–161, fisheries vulnerability and adaptation assessment.
claims.paraphrase: TNC relays a literature-based hypothesis that climate change may shift purse-seine tuna zones beyond Seychelles’ EEZ, reducing Port Victoria’s attractiveness and affecting fishing livelihoods and fish supply.
claims.scenario: Emissions pathway not specified by cited hypothesis.
affected_groups: people relying on fish as protein
claims.limitations: This is a cited hypothesis, not evidence of an observed tuna shift.

claims.locator: TNC printed p. 30, health-sector risks and adaptation barriers.
claims.paraphrase: TNC says most primary-care facilities are low-lying and often flooded during heavy rain, interrupting services; limited land constrains relocation and shoreline setbacks.
claims.limitations: The communication provides no facility list or district-level count.

claims.locator: UNDP article, opening paragraph, 9 July 2026 handover.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP, the Government and China CIDCA handed 35 tablets to DRDM for more efficient real-time disaster and climate-hazard data collection and sharing.
institutions: Department of Risk and Disaster Management
claims.limitations: The handover is an institutional input, not evidence of improved warning outcomes.

claims.locator: UNDP article, “Strengthening Disaster Risk Management through Technology” and TIAEWS description.
claims.paraphrase: TIAEWS aims to implement an integrated disaster-information system, improve real-time warnings and crisis communication, and connect communities with first responders.
institutions: Department of Risk and Disaster Management
claims.limitations: These are stated project aims; the article reports no implementation or outcome evaluation.

claims.locator: DRDM “About Us,” institutional history and mandate.
claims.paraphrase: The department says the Disaster Risk Management Division became a Principal-Secretary-led DRDM under the Vice-President in December 2025, aiming to strengthen governance and operational coordination.
institutions: Department of Risk and Disaster Management
claims.limitations: The department's description states institutional aims, not measured performance.

claims.locator: UNDP CPD official webpage, theory-of-change extract.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP’s 2024–28 programme plans to embed ecosystem-service valuation in sector plans to build climate resilience and early warning, manage resources, and support alternative livelihoods for women in fisher communities and at-risk or underemployed youth.
claims.limitations: This is a programme theory of change, not evidence of delivered benefits.

access_audit.locator: Full 90-page CCDR directly read; Executive Summary, road-network, social-protection and water sections inspected.
access_audit.notes: Directly read publisher-hosted PDF passages, including caveats on household-risk indicators and scenario modeling.
access_audit.reuse_terms: World Bank permits noncommercial reproduction with attribution, subject to third-party permissions.

access_audit.locator: Full 327-page Third National Communication directly read; rainfall projections, coastal vulnerability, health, fisheries and adaptation sections inspected.
access_audit.notes: Directly read official UNFCCC-hosted government PDF; cited figures and claims are qualified by the report's own methods and limitations.

access_audit.locator: Official UNDP article body, 10 July 2026, handover and TIAEWS paragraphs.
access_audit.notes: Full publisher-page body was read; the stated system goals remain plans, not evaluated effects.

access_audit.locator: Official DRDM About Us page, institutional history, mandate and mission.
access_audit.notes: Directly read official departmental page; institutional objectives are attributed to the department.

access_audit.locator: Official UNDP publication landing page, dated 22 May 2024, programme theory-of-change extract.
access_audit.notes: Only the official landing-page excerpt was read; it supports intended programme design, not delivered outputs.

search_audit.query: Seychelles climate change subnational vulnerability coastal erosion flooding Mahé Praslin La Digue government report PDF
search_audit.outcome: Read the 2026 CCDR and 2023 TNC. Verified named road, beach and rainfall-zone examples; a household-risk table has an inconsistent prose/table denominator and is qualified.

search_audit.query: Seychelles climate change conflict violence security livelihood displacement climate security report
search_audit.outcome: Search returned no Seychelles-specific primary evidence of climate-related organized violence or conflict. The CCDR discusses household financial strain and displacement after climate-related disasters, not conflict displacement.

search_audit.query: Seychelles conflict legacy climate adaptation security reverse climate FCV government report
search_audit.outcome: No country-specific primary source found linking conflict or violence to constrained adaptation; this is a search gap, not evidence of absence.

search_audit.query: Seychelles climate resilience capacity adaptation disaster risk early warning government UNDP report
search_audit.outcome: Read current UNDP and DRDM official pages plus the 2024–28 UNDP programme excerpt; verified a 2026 data-collection handover, stated TIAEWS functions and the 2025 institutional transformation.

gaps: No directly inspected Seychelles-specific primary source established climate-to-armed-conflict or organized-violence causation, or conflict-to-adaptation constraint; this remains a search gap, not evidence of absence.
Seychelles was absent from EXISTING_COUNTRIES.json, so there was no listed country baseline to compare.
